{{Infobox ancient site |name = Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun |location = {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}{{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}} Ōsawa 2-chome |coordinates = {{coordinates|35|40|26.6|N|139|32|20.1|E|scale:10000}} |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = Tier 1: 27–28 m square
Tier 2: 18 m diameter
Height: 2.2 m |burial_facility = Multi-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} third quarter |buried_individual = |artifacts = Haji ware, Sue ware |designated_cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map = Japan Tokyo |icon = 上円下方墳 |label = |label_position = bottom |image = [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun, funkyu with railing and sign - 2022.jpg|280px]]
Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Kofun in Tokyo]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:History of Mitaka]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Jōen-kahō-fun]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[ja:天文台構内古墳]] {{draft categories| [[Category:dd]][[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:removed redirect]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:bump 1-20 (2)]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:bump 1-26]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:properly attributed pages]][[Category:{Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] [[Category:CategoryCategory]] [[Category:CategoryCategoryk]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] {{Kofun navbar}} [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] [[Category:from everydodywiki with needed marking of original title]] }} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}}{{draft}} {{Promising draft|reason=the high amount of work put into it over a long time, see edit history}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site |name = Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun |location = {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}{{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}} Ōsawa 2-chome |coordinates = {{coordinates|35|40|26.6|N|139|32|20.1|E|scale:10000}} |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = Tier 1: 27–28 m square
Tier 2: 18 m diameter
Height: 2.2 m |burial_facility = Multi-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} third quarter |buried_individual = |artifacts = Haji ware, Sue ware |designated_cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map = Japan Tokyo |icon = 上円下方墳 |label = |label_position = bottom |image = [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun, funkyu with railing and sign - 2022.jpg|280px]]
Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Kofun in Tokyo]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:History of Mitaka]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Jōen-kahō-fun]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[ja:天文台構内古墳]] {{draft categories| [[Category:dd]][[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Kofun in Japan]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:removed redirect]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:attempting to force efresh]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:dd]][[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:bump 1-20 (2)]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:bump 1-26]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:properly attributed pages]][[Category:{Tenmondai Kofun]][[Category:dd]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] [[Category:CategoryCategory]] [[Category:CategoryCategoryk]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] {{Kofun navbar}} [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]][[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]][[Category:Pages from everybodywiki under right title]] [[Category:kk]][[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]][[Category:kk]] }} {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Source Wikipedia}}

Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site |name = Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun |location = {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}{{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}} Ōsawa 2-chome |coordinates = {{coordinates|35|40|26.6|N|139|32|20.1|E|scale:10000}} |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = Tier 1: 27–28 m square
Tier 2: 18 m diameter
Height: 2.2 m |burial_facility = Multi-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} third quarter |buried_individual = |artifacts = Haji ware, Sue ware |designated_cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map = Japan Tokyo |icon = 上円下方墳 |label = |label_position = bottom |image = [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun, funkyu with railing and sign - 2022.jpg|280px]]
Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] [[Category:dd]][[Category:Kofun in Tokyo]] [[Category:dd]][[Category:History Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site |name = Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun |location = {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}} {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}} Ōsawa 2-chome |coordinates = {{coordinates|35|40|26.6|N|139|32|20.1|E|scale:10000}} |shape = {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}} |size = Tier 1: 27–28 m square
Tier 2: 18 m diameter
Height: 2.2 m |burial_facility = Multi-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |construction_period = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} third quarter |buried_individual = |artifacts = Haji ware, Sue ware |designated_cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map = Japan Tokyo |icon = 上円下方墳 |label = |label_position = bottom |image = [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun, funkyu with railing and sign - 2022.jpg|280px]]
Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its shape is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳}}, but it has not been designated as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry platform for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue ware|ja|須恵器}} jars and {{ill|Haji ware|ja|土師器}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Yokoana Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == Burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|Burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the former. == Artifacts == Artifacts include Haji ware and Sue ware unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue ware has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == Related Topics == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of
