Tier 2: 18 m diameter
Height: 2.2 m |burial = Multi-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} |built = {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}} third quarter |Interred_individual = |burial goods = Haji pottery, Sue pottery |other_designation1_cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map = Japan Tokyo |type = 上円下方墳 |map_dot_label = |map_dot_label = bottom |image = [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun, funkyu with railing and sign - 2022.jpg|280px]]
Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been other_designation1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-Period Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-Period Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} * {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] [[Category:11]][[Category:Kofun in Tokyo]] [[Category:11]][[Category:History Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been other_designation1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been other_designation1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been other_designation1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been other_designation1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been other_designation1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of Mound }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス}} premises in {{ill|Mitaka, Tokyo|ja|三鷹市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a {{ill|Fujizuka|ja|富士塚}} in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the {{ill|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|ja|東京都教育委員会}} carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}, which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of {{ill|Sue pottery|ja|須恵器|1=Sue pottery}} jars and {{ill|Haji pottery|ja|土師器|1=Haji pottery}} bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Cave Tomb Group|ja|出山横穴墓群}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}} and {{ill|Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the {{ill|7th century|ja|7世紀}}, matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the {{ill|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|ja|武蔵府中熊野神社古墳}}. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and Construction of {{日本の古墳 |名称=天文台構内古墳 |所在地=[[東京都]][[三鷹市]]大沢2丁目 |位置={{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|40|26.6|N|139|32|20.1|E|scale:10000}} |形状=[[上円下方墳]] |規模=第1段：一辺27-28m
第2段：直径18m
高さ2.2m |埋葬施設=複室構造[[横穴式石室]] |築造年代=[[7世紀]]第三四半期 |被葬者= |出土品=土師器、須恵器 |指定文化財= |特記事項= |地図 =Japan Tokyo |アイコン =上円下方墳 |ラベル = |ラベル位置 =bottom |画像=[[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun, funkyu with railing and sign - 2022.jpg|280px]]
墳丘 }} '''天文台構内古墳'''（てんもんだいこうないこふん）は、[[東京都]][[三鷹市]][[大沢 (三鷹市)|大沢]]の[[国立天文台三鷹キャンパス]]敷地内にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[上円下方墳]]。史跡指定はされていない。 ==古墳発見と発掘の経緯== 天文台構内古墳は、[[江戸時代]]後期の地誌『[[新編武蔵風土記稿]]』と『[[武蔵名勝図会]]』の、[[多摩郡]]世田谷領大沢村の項に[[富士塚]]として記載されており{{sfn|新編武蔵風土記稿|1929|page=346}}、当時は富士塚として利用されていたことが明らかになっている。また当時は[[女人禁制]]で婦女子が登ることが禁じられており、その昔、[[甲府徳川家|甲府殿]]の[[鷹狩|鷹場]]の御立場として利用されたという[[伝承|言い伝え]]があるとの記述もある{{sfn|新編武蔵風土記稿|1929|page=346}}。 このように天文台構内古墳は長い間[[古墳]]とはみなされていなかったが、[[1970年]]（昭和45年）、三鷹市の市史編纂委員会の手によって発掘が行われ、[[横穴式石室]]の存在が明らかになり古墳であることが判明した。ただし学界に[[発掘調査]]の成果が公表されず、古墳の存在も広く知られることがなかった。 [[1992年]]（平成4年）から[[1994年]]（平成6年）にかけて、[[東京都]][[教育委員会]]が[[多摩]]地区の古墳について確認調査を実施し、その報告書の中で初めて天文台構内古墳の名が学会に知られるようになった。 [[2003年]]（平成15年）から開始された[[武蔵府中熊野神社古墳]]の発掘の結果、よく似た[[横穴式石室]]を持っている天文台構内古墳の注目度が高まったこともあって、天文台構内古墳は[[2004年]]（平成16年）度以降、継続して[[発掘調査]]・研究が行われている。 まず[[2004年]]12月、天文台構内古墳の墳丘測量調査が実施された。その後[[2006年]]（平成18年）2月には横穴式石室の全容調査を目的とした発掘調査が行われ、複室・胴張り形の[[石室]]であることが確認された。2006年11月の発掘調査では墳丘の状態と周濠について確認がなされた。 さらに[[2007年]]（平成19年）10月から11月にかけて墳丘や墳丘周囲の発掘調査が行われ、その結果2007年12月、天文台構内古墳は全国4例目の上円下方墳であることが判明した。ただし下方部に墳丘・[[葺石]]をほどこした武蔵府中熊野神社古墳と異なり、天文台構内古墳は円墳の周囲に方形の周濠がめぐっている形をしており、上円下方墳の類型の墳型として「方基円墳」という名称も提唱されている池上（2008）pp84-86.。 [[2008年]]（平成20年）8月、[[玄室]]内から[[7世紀]]第三四半期のものと見られる[[須恵器]]の[[壺]]と、[[土師器]]の坏が発見された。 ==古墳の立地== 天文台構内古墳は[[武蔵野台地]]上にあり、古墳の北西から南東側には[[野川 (東京都)|野川]]北岸沿いに[[河岸段丘]]である[[国分寺崖線]]がある。また古墳の東側には野川に注ぐ支流が刻んだ谷があり、天文台構内古墳は武蔵野台地の辺縁部に位置している。墳丘の南側には小さな谷があり、古墳全体としても南側がやや低くなっている。 三鷹市内の野川流域とその近隣には、[[出山横穴墓群]]など七群の[[横穴墓]]群があり[http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/kikaku4/yokoana1.htm 特集みたかの横穴墓]、うち六群の横穴墓群は国分寺崖線に沿って造られている。天文台構内古墳東側にある谷沿いにも原横穴墓群があるなど、古墳周辺には数多くの横穴墓が造られているが、天文台構内古墳の周辺には高塚式の古墳は存在しない。 国立天文台三鷹キャンパス内には、[[旧石器時代 (日本)|旧石器時代]]から[[近世]]までの複合遺跡である天文台構内遺跡がある。もともとこの地域は豊かな[[湧水]]に恵まれており、水利に恵まれ生活に適した場所であった。 ==墳丘について== 一辺27 - 28メートルの方墳の上に、直径約18メートル、高さ2.2メートルの円墳が乗った形の上円下方墳。もともと上円部の高さは3.7メートル程度あったものと推定されている。古墳の東側、北側、西側には最大幅7.5メートル、深さ1.8メートルになる周濠があるが、周濠の深さ、幅とも不整形である。なお、墳丘南側に周濠がめぐっているかどうかまだ不明である。 葺石については墳丘の一部に確認されている[http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/jousetsu2/0313_20.htm 古墳時代のみたか]。かつては墳丘全体を覆っていたものと思われる。 墳丘は[[関東ローム]]や黒土を互い違いに突き固める[[版築]]工法で造成されていた。 ==古墳の主体部== [[画像:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|天文台構内古墳の墓前域と石室上部。]] 天文台構内古墳の主体部は、[[羨道]]、前室、玄室の三室構造の横穴式石室であり、全長は約6.9メートルである。墓前域は八の字に開き、玄室は丸みを帯びた胴張り形である。また石室は極めて軟らかい[[シルト岩]]を組み合わせて造られている。[[1970年]]（昭和45年）の発掘調査では、石室の床面は河原石で敷石がなされているのが確認されている。 これらの特徴は東京都多摩地区の終末期古墳である、[[府中市 (東京都)|府中市]]の[[武蔵府中熊野神社古墳]]や[[八王子市]]の[[北大谷古墳]]などと一致しており、特に武蔵府中熊野神社古墳との類似性が注目されるが、主体部基礎の掘り込み地業は約40センチメートルと、1.5メートル以上の掘り込み地業が行われていた武蔵府中熊野神社古墳との大きな違いもある。 1970年の発掘調査では[[玄室]]の存在が確認されておらず、2006年2月の発掘調査の結果、初めて胴張り形をした玄室の存在が明らかとなった。玄室部分の天井石は全て崩落しており、現在、玄室は埋まった状態になっている。2008年度には玄室内の発掘調査が行われた。 ==出土品== 古墳の主体部の発掘がまだ終了していないため、現在のところ出土品は周濠、そして玄室から出土した[[須恵器]]と[[土師器]]のみである。玄室内から発掘された須恵器は[[7世紀]]第三四半期のものと見られ、石室の形態から判断される古墳築造時期とほぼ一致している。 ==古墳の特徴== 天文台構内古墳の特徴としては、まず全国で4例目となる上円下方墳であることが挙げられる。石室の形態などから築造時期は7世紀半ばから後半にかけてと考えられている。約7.5キロメートル西側にある上円下方墳の武蔵府中熊野神社古墳との類似性が注目されるところであるが、古墳の規模などから判断すると、天文台構内古墳は多摩地区において、武蔵府中熊野神社古墳に次ぐ位置を占めた古墳であると考えられる。天文台構内古墳は石室の形態から、武蔵府中熊野神社古墳の少し後に築造されたと考える研究者が多い小野本（2008）p.20、青木（2009）p.80。 また天文台構内古墳は、[[八王子市]]の[[北大谷古墳]]や武蔵府中熊野神社古墳と同様の、複室・胴張り形の石室を持っており、このような特徴を持った多摩地域の終末期古墳は、同時期の他の多摩地域の古墳と比べて明らかに規模が大きく、多摩地域の首長の中でも有力者を葬る形式の古墳として定着していたものと考えられる。複室・胴張り形の石室は、[[九州地方]]北部の[[筑後国|筑後]]地域の6世紀後半以降の古墳でよく見られる特徴であり、北部九州の古墳の影響を受けて6世紀末以降、[[武蔵国|武蔵]]北部や南武蔵の[[多摩川]]流域で複室・胴張り形の石室を持つ古墳の築造が始まったとの説も唱えられている{{sfn|『関東の後期古墳群』|pp=112,121}}。 天文台構内古墳の近隣には数多くの横穴墓があり、それら横穴墓が造られた時期は7世紀中ごろから後半以降とみられている。天文台構内古墳の被葬者は、横穴墓を造った集団を支配する地位にある、多摩地区でも有力な首長であったと考えられる。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == *『武蔵名勝図会』慶友社、1975年 *三鷹市史編纂委員会『三鷹市史』三鷹市、1970年 *多摩地区所在古墳確認調査団『多摩地区所在古墳確認調査報告書』、1995年。 *『[[大日本地誌大系]]13　新編武蔵風土記稿第七巻』[[雄山閣]]、1996年 *{{cite book|和書|title=大日本地誌大系|volume=第10巻 新編武蔵風土記稿6|chapter=巻ノ126多磨郡ノ38大沢村|id={{NDLJP|1214867/178}}|publisher=雄山閣|editor=蘆田伊人編|date=1929-8|page=346|ref={{sfnref|新編武蔵風土記稿|1929}}}} *[[品川区立品川歴史館|品川区品川歴史館]]編『東京の古墳を考える』雄山閣、2006年。 *「武蔵と相模の古墳」（『季刊考古学』別冊15）雄山閣、2007年。 *{{cite book|和書|title=関東の後期古墳群|publisher=[[六一書房]]|year=2007|editor=佐々木憲一 編|isbn=9784947743558|series=考古学リーダー 12|ref={{sfnref|『関東の後期古墳群』}}}} *池上悟「上円下方墳の名称と築造企画」『白門考古論叢II』中央考古会・中央大学考古学研究会、2008年。 *小野本敦「流通路から見た武蔵の後・終末期古墳」『東京考古26』東京考古談話会、2008年 *青木敬「多摩地区における7世紀の古墳」『東京考古27』東京考古談話会、2009年 == 関連項目 == * [[武蔵府中熊野神社古墳]] * [[北大谷古墳]] * [[国立天文台三鷹キャンパス]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} *[http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html 天文台構内古墳は多摩川上流域における首長墓　三鷹市のホームページ]{{リンク切れ|date=2019-12-18}} (東京都)|野川]]北岸沿いに[[河岸段丘]]である[[国分寺崖線]]がある。また古墳の東側には野川に注ぐ支流が刻んだ谷があり、天文台構内古墳は武蔵野台地の辺縁部に位置している。墳丘の南側には小さな谷があり、古墳全体としても南側がやや低くなっている。 三鷹市内の野川流域とその近隣には、[[出山横穴墓群]]など七群の[[横穴墓]]群があり[http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/kikaku4/yokoana1.htm 特集みたかの横穴墓]、うち六群の横穴墓群は国分寺崖線に沿って造られている。天文台構内古墳東側にある谷沿いにも原横穴墓群があるなど、古墳周辺には数多くの横穴墓が造られているが、天文台構内古墳の周辺には高塚式の古墳は存在しない。 国立天文台三鷹キャンパス内には、[[旧石器時代 (日本)|旧石器時代]]から[[近世]]までの複合遺跡である天文台構内遺跡がある。もともとこの地域は豊かな[[湧水]]に恵まれており、水利に恵まれ生活に適した場所であった。 ==墳丘について== 一辺27 - 28メートルの方墳の上に、直径約18メートル、高さ2.2メートルの円墳が乗った形の上円下方墳。もともと上円部の高さは3.7メートル程度あったものと推定されている。古墳の東側、北側、西側には最大幅7.5メートル、深さ1.8メートルになる周濠があるが、周濠の深さ、幅とも不整形である。なお、墳丘南側に周濠がめぐっているかどうかまだ不明である。 葺石については墳丘の一部に確認されている[http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/jousetsu2/0313_20.htm 古墳時代のみたか]。かつては墳丘全体を覆っていたものと思われる。 墳丘は[[関東ローム]]や黒土を互い違いに突き固める[[版築]]工法で造成されていた。 ==古墳の主体部== [[画像:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|天文台構内古墳の墓前域と石室上部。]] 天文台構内古墳の主体部は、[[羨道]]、前室、玄室の三室構造の横穴式石室であり、全長は約6.9メートルである。墓前域は八の字に開き、玄室は丸みを帯びた胴張り形である。また石室は極めて軟らかい[[シルト岩]]を組み合わせて造られている。[[1970年]]（昭和45年）の発掘調査では、石室の床面は河原石で敷石がなされているのが確認されている。 これらの特徴は東京都多摩地区の終末期古墳である、[[府中市 (東京都)|府中市]]の[[武蔵府中熊野神社古墳]]や[[八王子市]]の[[北大谷古墳]]などと一致しており、特に武蔵府中熊野神社古墳との類似性が注目されるが、主体部基礎の掘り込み地業は約40センチメートルと、1.5メートル以上の掘り込み地業が行われていた武蔵府中熊野神社古墳との大きな違いもある。 1970年の発掘調査では[[玄室]]の存在が確認されておらず、2006年2月の発掘調査の結果、初めて胴張り形をした玄室の存在が明らかとなった。玄室部分の天井石は全て崩落しており、現在、玄室は埋まった状態になっている。2008年度には玄室内の発掘調査が行われた。 ==出土品== 古墳の主体部の発掘がまだ終了していないため、現在のところ出土品は周濠、そして玄室から出土した[[須恵器]]と[[土師器]]のみである。玄室内から発掘された須恵器は[[7世紀]]第三四半期のものと見られ、石室の形態から判断される古墳築造時期とほぼ一致している。 ==古墳の特徴== 天文台構内古墳の特徴としては、まず全国で4例目となる上円下方墳であることが挙げられる。石室の形態などから築造時期は7世紀半ばから後半にかけてと考えられている。約7.5キロメートル西側にある上円下方墳の武蔵府中熊野神社古墳との類似性が注目されるところであるが、古墳の規模などから判断すると、天文台構内古墳は多摩地区において、武蔵府中熊野神社古墳に次ぐ位置を占めた古墳であると考えられる。天文台構内古墳は石室の形態から、武蔵府中熊野神社古墳の少し後に築造されたと考える研究者が多い小野本（2008）p.20、青木（2009）p.80。 また天文台構内古墳は、[[八王子市]]の[[北大谷古墳]]や武蔵府中熊野神社古墳と同様の、複室・胴張り形の石室を持っており、このような特徴を持った多摩地域の終末期古墳は、同時期の他の多摩地域の古墳と比べて明らかに規模が大きく、多摩地域の首長の中でも有力者を葬る形式の古墳として定着していたものと考えられる。複室・胴張り形の石室は、[[九州地方]]北部の[[筑後国|筑後]]地域の6世紀後半以降の古墳でよく見られる特徴であり、北部九州の古墳の影響を受けて6世紀末以降、[[武蔵国|武蔵]]北部や南武蔵の[[多摩川]]流域で複室・胴張り形の石室を持つ古墳の築造が始まったとの説も唱えられている{{sfn|『関東の後期古墳群』|pp=112,121}}。 天文台構内古墳の近隣には数多くの横穴墓があり、それら横穴墓が造られた時期は7世紀中ごろから後半以降とみられている。天文台構内古墳の被葬者は、横穴墓を造った集団を支配する地位にある、多摩地区でも有力な首長であったと考えられる。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == *『武蔵名勝図会』慶友社、1975年 *三鷹市史編纂委員会『三鷹市史』三鷹市、1970年 *多摩地区所在古墳確認調査団『多摩地区所在古墳確認調査報告書』、1995年。 *『[[大日本地誌大系]]13　新編武蔵風土記稿第七巻』[[雄山閣]]、1996年 *{{cite book|和書|title=大日本地誌大系|volume=第10巻 新編武蔵風土記稿6|chapter=巻ノ126多磨郡ノ38大沢村|id={{NDLJP|1214867/178}}|publisher=雄山閣|editor=蘆田伊人編|date=1929-8|page=346|ref={{sfnref|新編武蔵風土記稿|1929}}}} *[[品川区立品川歴史館|品川区品川歴史館]]編『東京の古墳を考える』雄山閣、2006年。 *「武蔵と相模の古墳」（『季刊考古学』別冊15）雄山閣、2007年。 *{{cite book|和書|title=関東の後期古墳群|publisher=[[六一書房]]|year=2007|editor=佐々木憲一 編|isbn=9784947743558|series=考古学リーダー 12|ref={{sfnref|『関東の後期古墳群』}}}} *池上悟「上円下方墳の名称と築造企画」『白門考古論叢II』中央考古会・中央大学考古学研究会、2008年。 *小野本敦「流通路から見た武蔵の後・終末期古墳」『東京考古26』東京考古談話会、2008年 *青木敬「多摩地区における7世紀の古墳」『東京考古27』東京考古談話会、2009年 == 関連項目 == * [[武蔵府中熊野神社古墳]] * [[北大谷古墳]] * [[国立天文台三鷹キャンパス]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} *[http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html 天文台構内古墳は多摩川上流域における首長墓　三鷹市のホームページ]{{リンク切れ|date=2019-12-18}} *[http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/sekishitu.htm 石室の形態が明らかに、天文台構内古墳の発掘調査　みたか遺跡展示室] *[http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm 今年の発掘成果が期待される天文台構内古墳　みたか遺跡展示室] {{DEFAULTSORT:てんもんたいこうないこふん}}
