Tier 2: 18 m diameter
Height: 2.2 m |burial = Multi-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |built = [[:en:7th century|7th century]] third quarter |Interred_individual = |burial goods = Haji pottery, Sue pottery |Historic Site1_cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map = Japan Tokyo |type = 上円下方墳 |map_dot_label = |map_dot_label = bottom |image = [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun, funkyu with railing and sign - 2022.jpg|280px]]
Mound |architectural_styles = {{ill|round-topped burial mound|qid=Q11358496}} }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} premises in [[:en:Mitaka, Tokyo|Mitaka, Tokyo]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]]. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōen-kahō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a [[:en:Fujizuka|Fujizuka]] in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|qq=|1=Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11503943}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Meisho Zue|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名所図会の一覧|1=list of meisho zue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11415434}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Tokugawa Family|qq=|1=Kōfu-Tokugawa family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577816}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the [[:en:Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education]] carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] jars and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]] bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]]. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the [[:en:Musashino Plateau|Musashino Plateau]]. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogawa River|qq=|1=Nogawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11645425}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Graves|ja|出山横穴墓群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deyama Cave Tomb Group|qq=}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] and {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]], matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]]. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}}

Mound |architectural_styles = {{ill|round-topped burial mound|qid=Q11358496}} }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} premises in [[:en:Mitaka, Tokyo|Mitaka, Tokyo]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]]. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōen-kahō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a [[:en:Fujizuka|Fujizuka]] in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|qq=|1=Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11503943}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Meisho Zue|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名所図会の一覧|1=list of meisho zue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11415434}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Tokugawa Family|qq=|1=Kōfu-Tokugawa family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577816}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the [[:en:Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education]] carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] jars and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]] bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]]. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the [[:en:Musashino Plateau|Musashino Plateau]]. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogawa River|qq=|1=Nogawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11645425}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Graves|ja|出山横穴墓群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deyama Cave Tomb Group|qq=}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] and {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]], matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]]. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}}

Mound |architectural_styles = {{ill|round-topped burial mound|WD=Q11358496}} }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} premises in [[:en:Mitaka, Tokyo|Mitaka, Tokyo]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]]. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōen-kahō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a [[:en:Fujizuka|Fujizuka]] in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|qq=|1=Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11503943}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Meisho Zue|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名所図会の一覧|1=list of meisho zue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11415434}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Tokugawa Family|qq=|1=Kōfu-Tokugawa family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577816}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the [[:en:Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education]] carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] jars and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]] bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]]. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the [[:en:Musashino Plateau|Musashino Plateau]]. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogawa River|qq=|1=Nogawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11645425}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Graves|ja|出山横穴墓群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deyama Cave Tomb Group|qq=}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] and {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]], matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]]. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}}

The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}}

Mound |architectural_styles = {{ill|round-topped burial mound|WD=Q11358496}} }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} premises in [[:en:Mitaka, Tokyo|Mitaka, Tokyo]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]]. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōen-kahō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a [[:en:Fujizuka|Fujizuka]] in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1=Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11503943}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名所図会の一覧|1=list of meisho zue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11415434}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Tokugawa Family|1=Kōfu-Tokugawa family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577816}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the [[:en:Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education]] carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] jars and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]] bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]]. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the [[:en:Musashino Plateau|Musashino Plateau]]. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogawa River|1=Nogawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11645425}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Graves|ja|出山横穴墓群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deyama Cave Tomb Group|qq=}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] and {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]], matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]]. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}}

Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōen-kahō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a [[:en:Fujizuka|Fujizuka]] in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1=Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11503943}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名所図会の一覧|1=list of meisho zue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11415434}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Tokugawa Family|1=Kōfu-Tokugawa family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577816}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the [[:en:Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education]] carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] jars and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]] bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]]. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the [[:en:Musashino Plateau|Musashino Plateau]]. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogawa River|1=Nogawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11645425}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Graves|ja|出山横穴墓群|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deyama Cave Tomb Group|qq=}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] and {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]], matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]]. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}}

The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}}

Tier 2: 18 m diameter
Height: 2.2 m |burial = Multi-chambered {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} |built = [[:en:7th century|7th century]] third quarter |Interred_individual = |burial goods = Haji pottery, Sue pottery |Historic Site1_cultural_properties = |special_notes = |map = Japan Tokyo |type = 上円下方墳 |map_dot_label = |map_dot_label = bottom |image = [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun, funkyu with railing and sign - 2022.jpg|280px]]
Mound |architectural_styles = {{ill|round-topped burial mound|WD=Q11358496}} }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} premises in [[:en:Mitaka, Tokyo|Mitaka, Tokyo]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]]. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōen-kahō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a [[:en:Fujizuka|Fujizuka]] in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1=Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11503943}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名所図会の一覧|1=list of meisho zue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11415434}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Tokugawa Family|1=Kōfu-Tokugawa family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577816}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the [[:en:Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education]] carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] jars and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]] bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]]. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the [[:en:Musashino Plateau|Musashino Plateau]]. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogawa River|1=Nogawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11645425}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Graves|ja|出山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deyama Cave Tomb Group|qq=}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] and {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]], matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]]. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}} [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Tokugawa Family|1=Kōfu-Tokugawa family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577816}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the [[:en:Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education]] carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] jars and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]] bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]]. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the [[:en:Musashino Plateau|Musashino Plateau]]. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogawa River|1=Nogawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11645425}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Graves|ja|出山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deyama Cave Tomb Group|qq=}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] and {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]], matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]]. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun - City of Mitaka Official Website] * [http://www.mitaka-iseki.jp/sokuho5/jouenkakouhun.htm Excavation Reports - Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room] {{⚠️🚨COPIED from EverybodyWiki ❗❕⚠️😡😤Please respect Licence CC-BY-SA ❗}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|天文台構内古墳|version=100088490|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] }} [[Category:Everybody linked]] {{everybodywiki link|Tenmondai Kounai Kofun}} [[ceb:Tenmondai Kounai Kofun]] [[ja:天文台構内古墳]] [[Category:everybodywiki import successful]][[Category:everybodywiki import successful]] [[Category:History of Mitaka, Tokyo]] [[Category:Joenkahofun]] [[Category:Fujizuka]] [[Category:Kofun of Tokyo]] {{Commons category|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11442651}} [[Category:Wikidata no short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]]

Mound |architectural_styles = {{ill|round-topped burial mound|WD=Q11358496}} }} '''Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun''' (天文台構内古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] located in the {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} premises in [[:en:Mitaka, Tokyo|Mitaka, Tokyo]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]]. Its type is a {{ill|Jōen-kahō-fun|ja|上円下方墳|1=Joenkahofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōen-kahō-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Joenkahofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, but it has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site. == Discovery and Excavation == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was originally described as a [[:en:Fujizuka|Fujizuka]] in the Edo-period topographies {{ill|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|ja|新編武蔵風土記稿|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1=Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11503943}} and {{ill|Musashi Meisho Zue|ja|武蔵名勝図会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi Meisho Zue|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名所図会の一覧|1=list of meisho zue|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11415434}}, where it is listed under "Ōsawa Village, Setagaya Domain, Tama District."{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} It is noted to have been used as a Fujizuka at that time and restricted to men only, with women being prohibited from climbing it. Legends also mention its use as a falconry plattype for the {{ill|Kōfu Tokugawa Family|ja|甲府徳川家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Tokugawa Family|1=Kōfu-Tokugawa family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11577816}}.{{sfn|Shinpen Musashi Fudoki Kō|1929|page=346}} Though not recognized as a kofun for a long time, in 1970 the Mitaka City History Compilation Committee conducted an excavation, revealing the presence of a {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}} and confirming it as a kofun. However, the excavation results were not widely published, leaving the kofun largely unknown. From 1992 to 1994, the [[:en:Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education|Tokyo Metropolitan Government Board of Education]] carried out a survey of kofun in the Tama region, and Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun was first introduced to the academic community in their report. Renewed interest came in 2003 with the excavation of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a similar {{ill|Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|ja|横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|2=ja|3=横穴式石室|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|4=zh|5=橫穴式石室|6=ko|7=굴식 돌방무덤|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|1=Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokoana-shiki sekishitsu|13=User:Immanuelle/Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|qq=}}. Consequently, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun has been the subject of continued excavation and research since 2004. In December 2004, a survey of the mound was conducted, followed by a comprehensive excavation of the burial chamber in February 2006, confirming a multi-chambered, barrel-shaped structure. The surrounding moat and mound conditions were further investigated in November 2006. Another excavation from October to November 2007 established Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun as the fourth known Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Unlike the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]], which has a base covered in stone, Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun features a rectangular moat encircling a circular mound, a subtype now proposed as "Hōki-enfun."{{sfn|Ikegami|2008|pp=84–86}} In August 2008, the discovery of [[:en:Sue pottery|Sue pottery]] jars and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]] bowls in the burial chamber dated the kofun to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]]. == location == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is situated on the edge of the [[:en:Musashino Plateau|Musashino Plateau]]. To its northwest and southeast lies the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} along the {{ill|Nogawa River|ja|野川|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogawa River|1=Nogawa River|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11645425}}, with tributary valleys nearby. A small valley lies to its south, slightly lowering the surrounding elevation. Several horizontal burial groups, including the {{ill|Deyama Graves|ja|出山横穴墓群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Deyama Cave Tomb Group|qq=}}, exist along the {{ill|Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja|国分寺崖線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokubunji Cliff Line|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵野台地|1=Musashino Plateau|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2616063}} near the kofun, but no other high-mound tombs are in its immediate vicinity. == Mound == The kofun comprises a 27–28-meter square lower tier topped by an 18-meter diameter, 2.2-meter tall circular upper tier. The upper tier's original height is estimated at 3.7 meters. A moat surrounds the north, east, and west sides, reaching a maximum width of 7.5 meters and depth of 1.8 meters, though it is irregularly shaped. The moat's extension to the south remains unclear. The mound was constructed using an alternating rammed earth technique (hanjiku), incorporating layers of Kanto loam and black soil. Traces of stone covering (fukiseki) have been found on part of the mound.{{sfn|Mitaka Archaeological Exhibit Room}} == burial Chamber == [[File:Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun excavation.jpg|thumb|250px|burial site and stone chamber of Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun.]] The burial chamber consists of a passage, an antechamber, and a main chamber, totaling 6.9 meters in length. The main chamber is barrel-shaped, with walls constructed from soft siltstone. A 1970 excavation confirmed river stones were used to pave the floor. The chamber closely resembles those of the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] and {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}}, suggesting it was constructed slightly later than the typeer. == burial goods == burial goods include Haji pottery and Sue pottery unearthed from the burial chamber and moat. The Sue pottery has been dated to the third quarter of the [[:en:7th century|7th century]], matching the estimated construction period of the kofun. == Features == Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun is the fourth known example of a Jōen-kahō-fun in Japan. Its construction is closely tied to other high-status tombs in the Tama region, such as the [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]]. The burial structure reflects influences from northern Kyushu, where similar chambers appeared in the late 6th century, suggesting a transmission of tomb-building techniques to the Tama region.{{sfn|Kantō Late-built Kofun|pp=112,121}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * {{Cite book|editor=|author=Ikegami Satoru|title=Concept and built of Jōen-kahō-fun|publisher=Chūō Archaeological Association|year=2008|pages=84–86|ref=}} * {{Cite book|editor=|author=|title=Late-built Kofun in Kantō|publisher=Rokuichi Shobō|year=2007|isbn=9784947743558|ref=}} == See Also == * [[:en:Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun|Musashi Fuchū Kumano Jinja Kofun]] * {{ill|Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaotani Kofun|lt=Kitaōya Kofun|ja|北大谷古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitaōya Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|ja|国立天文台三鷹キャンパス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Astronomical Observatory of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tenmondai-Kounai Kofun}} * [http://www.city.mitaka.tokyo.jp/a002/p003/g14/d00300769.html Tenmondai Kōnai Kofun -
